scope: New default adapter, opt-in synthetic conformance harness, example, pinned upstream canonical APIs and current design; existing SpiralCore codecs/storage unchanged.
observations: direction.rs:185-300 sends only existing bounded Frame encodings through real prepare_mailbox_envelope, authorize_route, authorize_outbound and PeerChannel::try_send. Trusted configuration supplies identities/routes; no arbitrary raw-write bypass or invented mailbox port exists.

direction.rs:303-369 bounds the encoded envelope before canonical decode, checks encryption key and signed binding routing fields, invokes canonical authenticated open, then validates Frame bytes/kind before installing authority. Exact capability/content/kind restrictions and expected sender verification key are retained. Receive-only directions need no remote signing key.

policy.rs checks a generation-counted current policy under a consistent policy-to-lease lock order. VerifiedFrame rechecks its generation and Endpoint reuses the authority hook. Policy replacement invalidates prior proofs and namespace leases. This is not a concurrent revocation/publication transaction; the README states that live-service gap.

Replay uses the upstream authenticated ReplayIdentity, rejects duplicates and refuses capacity exhaustion without eviction. Application retries require a fresh canonical envelope; replay state is process-local and restart is not durable mailbox admission. Sequence and traffic counters use checked arithmetic.

The library forbids unsafe code. Production adapter paths propagate typed errors and have no panic/unwrap path. Example-only internal JSON counter unwraps consume values produced by its own typed counter conversion, not attacker-provided data; fixed-dose arithmetic is bounded. No shell execution, credential logging or network listener was added.

conformance.rs is feature-gated and uses ephemeral fixture keys with actual upstream cryptography and bounded InMemoryPeerTransport. It derives initial context after a counted canonical scope probe, forwards requests in order, checks response transfer/sequence/kind, and reopens the existing durable Endpoint for exact readback.

mailbox_transfer.rs separately records frame and canonical-envelope bytes, checks both received/sent counts, times sequential process CPU through durable application acknowledgment, and charges setup/schema/base traffic. It verifies every retained original byte before removing only freshly created owned stores. No WAN, pure wire-time, full-system energy or guest-isolation claim is made.

Existing direct-vs-adapter frame comparison, canonical tamper/recipient/epoch/revocation/oversize/cancellation/queue tests, lost-reply recovery and ternary/Kuramoto/CA RuntimeSession conformance cover the requested boundaries. Existing production transfer/store source diff from b2dacc6 is empty.
explicit_live_deployment_limits: The trusted control plane must refresh current policy/time; the deterministic conformance fixture does not advance clock-driven expiry.
General verified reply handles, durable inbox/replay, admission/rate limits, key provisioning and epoch/boot lifecycle remain upstream/integration work.

The current synchronous send holds a policy mutex across connect/try_send. Future transports must avoid policy re-entry and define bounded blocking/cancellation; the reviewed in-memory path is bounded.
The selector still minimizes the earlier HTTP-body cost model, not proven minimum canonical-envelope bytes. Actual envelope overhead must be measured.
No dependency advisory-database audit, FIPS validation, CUI qualification, actual vsock guest or network transport acceptance is asserted.

observed_qualification.clippy_final: qualification/clippy-03.txt records successful completion; earlier diagnostics remain retained
observed_qualification.pending: Root-owned final default cargo check, release build, changed-file coverage and exact source/executable freeze remain prerequisites for measurement. Result arithmetic review follows retained campaign rows.
